sectors.name: Technology
themes: Indonesia's digital economy expansion, driven by rising internet penetration and e-commerce adoption, provides durable demand for local tech firms like MCAS and GPSO.
Global AI infrastructure buildout continues to boost US semiconductor and networking stocks (MU, CIEN, SMCI), with Indonesia as a beneficiary of supply chain shifts.
Regulatory clarity on data localization and fintech licensing in Indonesia supports long-term growth for tech platforms, reducing policy risk for investors.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's tech sector underperformed, but watch for selective catalysts: MCAS surged 30.82% on local e-commerce tailwinds, while US-listed MU and SMCI rose on AI memory demand. Focus on Indonesia-based digital economy plays and US semis exposed to AI capex, as structural growth remains intact despite near-term volatility.

Focus on niche lenders capitalizing on unbanked penetration and commodity-linked credit products, as aggregate sector signals normal with selective alpha in small caps.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's 75 GW renewable target by 2040, backed by President Prabowo's administration, creates a structural demand driver for solar, wind, and geothermal developers, with MPOW as a direct beneficia
The planned carbon tax and emissions trading scheme, delayed but imminent, will increase coal-fired power costs, accelerating corporate PPAs for renewables and boosting climate-tech solutions.
PLN's grid modernization and transmission expansion, funded by multilateral loans, are critical to unlocking utility-scale renewable projects, reducing curtailment risk for listed IPPs.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's renewables sector is underperforming US peers, but watch for policy catalysts: the new government's push for 75 GW renewable capacity by 2040 and upcoming carbon tax implementation could re-rate undervalued names like MPOW. Near-term, focus on project financing clarity and PLN's off-take agreements as key triggers.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Rising middle-class spending in Indonesia is structurally boosting demand for affordable packaged foods and personal care products, insulating domestic-focused FMCG firms from global headwinds.
Government policies promoting local manufacturing and raw material self-sufficiency are creating durable cost advantages for Indonesian consumer companies over import-dependent peers.
Digital distribution and direct-to-consumer channels are structurally expanding margins for nimble FMCG players, enabling them to capture market share from traditional retailers.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's consumer sector is flashing an ALERT signal with -1.62% aggregate decline, but selective FMCG names like AGAR (+24.75%) and PSDN (+11.21%) are surging on domestic demand resilience. This divergence suggests a rotation toward value plays and niche staples, not broad weakness. Position into mid-cap food/beverage and personal care stocks that benefit from stable local consumption, avoiding export-exposed names vulnerable to US slowdown (-1.72% US).

sectors.name: Property & Real Estate
themes: Jakarta's office oversupply (30%+ vacancy) will persist through 2025, crushing rental yields and forcing developers to write down land banks, a structural headwind for all but niche players.
Rising US 10-year yields are tightening global liquidity, directly pressuring Indonesian REITs and highly leveraged developers as foreign capital retreats to safer havens.
The government's IKN Nusantara relocation is diverting demand away from Greater Jakarta's residential and commercial property, creating a multi-year drag on core market absorption.
sectors.ai: Sell into today's BAPI-led bounce; the sector's -2.22% ID slide signals deepening distress, with US rate sensitivity and weak Jakarta absorption overwhelming any single-stock rallies. Rotate to cash or defensive subsectors like industrial/logistics REITs until clarity on BI's next move emerges.
